cultural_context.description: Tamil Nadu has a rich and diverse cultural heritage expressed through Tamil language and literature, temple architecture, classical and folk music and dance, festivals, crafts, cuisine, and regional traditions.
cultural_context.important_note: Cultural practices vary across regions, communities, religions, families, generations, and individual contexts. Information in this file should not be treated as universal to every person in Tamil Nadu.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Tamil Nadu

communication_guidance: Use respectful communication when interacting with local people.
Tamil Nadu has regional, linguistic, religious, and community diversity, so do not assume one communication style represents everyone.
When participating in a cultural or religious event, follow the guidance of local hosts, organizers, or the relevant venue.
greetings_and_communication.limitation: The current verified knowledge base does not contain a sufficiently sourced everyday Tamil phrase list. Do not invent Tamil phrases or translations.

verified_information.description: Official tourism material describes Tamil cuisine as diverse, with distinct culinary traditions across regions including Chettinad and Kongu areas. Rice, lentils, grains, vegetables, and a variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian preparations are part of the documented cuisine.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Tamil Nadu

verified_information.description: Official Incredible India material notes the traditional practice of serving meals on banana leaves as part of the dining culture of Tamil Nadu.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Tamil Nadu

verified_information.description: Pongal festival traditions include preparing and offering Pongal, a rice-based preparation, as part of harvest celebrations.

source.organization: Tamil Nadu Tourism
source.title: Thai Pongal Festival

dining_guidance: Do not assume one Tamil cuisine represents the entire state.
Food practices vary by region, community, religion, family tradition, and individual preference.
When invited to a traditional meal, observe local hosts and follow their guidance rather than assuming a particular dining custom is universal.
food_and_dining.limitation: The verified knowledge base does not establish universal everyday dining etiquette for every region and community in Tamil Nadu.

core_values.name: Cultural continuity
core_values.description: Tamil Nadu's cultural identity is reflected through its long literary, architectural, musical, dance, craft, and festival traditions.

festivals.name: Pongal
festivals.period: Usually January 13-16; dates follow the Tamil calendar
festivals.description: Pongal is a major harvest festival in Tamil Nadu. Official tourism sources describe the four-day observance through Bogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal, and Kaanum/Thiruvalluvar Day, with traditions involving the Sun, nature, agricultural harvests, and cattle.

source.organization: Tamil Nadu Tourism
source.title: Thai Pongal Festival

festivals.name: Puthandu
festivals.period: Usually mid-April; date varies according to the Tamil calendar
festivals.description: Puthandu is the Tamil New Year. Tourism material documents traditions including decorative Kolam designs and family or temple observances.

source.organization: Tamil Nadu Tourism
source.title: Most Important Festivals of Tamilnadu

festivals.name: Chithirai Festival
festivals.description: Chithirai celebrations are among the festivals documented by Tamil Nadu's Department of Art and Culture and state tourism material, with major traditions associated with Madurai.

festivals.name: Thyagaraja Aradhana

traditional_arts.description: Kolam is a traditional floor-art practice in which decorative designs are created at the entrance of homes. Official tourism material describes it as symbolizing welcome, prosperity, and blessings.

visitor_guidance: Treat temples, religious ceremonies, festivals, ritual performances, and community traditions with respect.
When entering temples or other sacred spaces, follow the venue's instructions regarding clothing, footwear, photography, and behavior.
Ask before photographing people, ritual performers, religious ceremonies, or culturally significant activities when permission or local rules are unclear.
Do not assume a festival or practice observed in one district or community applies throughout Tamil Nadu.
Respect Kolam and other household or community cultural practices rather than treating them merely as tourist photo opportunities.
Do not treat ritual or devotional performances simply as entertainment.
Tamil Nadu has significant regional diversity in cuisine, arts, festivals, and customs; avoid presenting one tradition as representative of everyone.
